Beállítom Ellenőrzött robbantással semmisítették meg azt a sérült drónt, amelyet kedden Románia keleti részén, a Moldovai Köztársaság határától mintegy 30 kilométerre találtak. A helyi Vaslui TV forrásai szerint a gép robbanótöltetet szállított. A drón eredetének hivatalos vizsgálata még tart. A gépre egy juhait legeltető pásztor bukkant rá a Vaslui megyei Viișoara település melletti mezőn. A beszámolók szerint oda is ment a drónhoz, és amikor az zümmögni kezdett, két vezetéket húzott ki belőle, robbanás azonban ekkor nem következett be. A férfi ezt követően hívta a 112-es segélyhívót. A helyi tévé szerint a drón ukrán gyártmányú lehetett, de a hatósági azonosítás még nem zárult le. Egyelőre azt sem tudni, honnan érkezett, mikor zuhant le, és mennyi ideig feküdt a mezőn. A rendőrséget kedd délelőtt negyed tizenegykor értesítették. Rendőrök és csendőrök zárták le a környéket, később pedig az eredetinél kétszer nagyobb területet ürítettek ki. A rendőrautókat is távolabb vitték, és egy munkagépet vezényeltek a helyszínre. Sérültekről nem érkezett hír. A HotNews szerint értesítették a Román Hírszerző Szolgálatot (SRI), amelynek tűzszerészei és terrorelhárítói is kimentek a helyszínre. Az ügyészség szintén vizsgálatot indított, hogy tisztázza a drón eredetét, és azt, hogyan került a mezőre. A felfedezés olyan napon történt, amikor Románia másik keleti határszakaszán is drónok miatt rendeltek el készültséget. Keddre virradóan orosz Sahed drónok megrongálták az ukrajnai Orlivka határátkelőt . Az átkelő a Duna ukrajnai partján, a folyó deltájának közelében található, innen komp jár a túlparton fekvő romániai Isaccea felé. Az ukrán határőrség szerint találatok érték az átkelő épületét és területét, több helyen pedig tűz ütött ki. Az átkelőt ideiglenesen bezárták, a kompforgalom leállt, a járműveket más határállomásokhoz irányítják. Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök szerint Oroszország szándékosan támadta meg az átkelőt, mert az Ukrajna exportját kiszolgáló útvonal része. A támadás idején a román hadsereg radarjai két légi célpontot észleltek az ukrán Vilkove közelében, nem messze a román határtól. A védelmi minisztérium közlése szerint a Fekete-tenger partjához közeli Mihail Kogălniceanu légibázisról két spanyol F–18-as vadászgép szállt fel. A spanyol gépek a NATO romániai légtérrendészeti missziójában vesznek részt. Később egy román katonai helikoptert is riasztottak. Tulcea megye északkeleti, Ukrajnával határos részén mobiltelefonos veszélyjelzést küldtek a lakosságnak. A vadászgépek pilótái Ukrajna felől robbanásokat láttak, a román védelmi minisztérium szerint azonban ezúttal nem sértették meg Románia légterét. Ugyanakkor Radu Miruță ügyvivő védelmi miniszter ugyanezen a reggelen jelentette be, hogy Szlovákia alacsonyan repülő drónok felderítésére alkalmas radarokat és ezeket kezelő katonákat küld Romániába . Bukarest korábban a NATO-tól és az Európai Uniótól is segítséget kért a keleti határ megfigyelésének megerősítéséhez. Az új radarokra azért van szükség, mert az alacsonyan repülő drónok az utóbbi hónapokban többször is észrevétlenül jutottak be Romániába. Augusztus 14-én egy drón úgy repült át a határon, és zuhant le Luncavița közelében , hogy a román hadsereg radarjai egyáltalán nem érzékelték. Hat nappal később egy másik drón már a radarok által követve lépett be Romániába, majd a Duna menti Grindu közelében zuhant le . Júliusban egy román F–16-os Bukaresttől mintegy 90 kilométerre lőtt le egy ismeretlen drónt , május végén pedig egy orosz Gerany–2 drón egy galaci lakóházba csapódott . Románia ezután gyors légvédelmi támogatást kért a NATO-tól. Augusztusban a Fekete-tengeren, a Neptun Deep gázmező közelében is két orosz drónt semmisítettek meg a román hatóságok. (AP Photo/Danylo Antoniuk) KYIV, Ukraine — Russia hammered Kyiv with drones in daylight attacks on Wednesday hours before Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with world leaders at the U.N. General Assembly. Two people were killed and 41 wounded in Ukraine’s capital as the attack stretched into Wednesday afternoon. Palls of black smoke floated above the city following the latest in what have been daily Russian attacks that torment Ukrainian civilians. The drones set off fires and damaged buildings in Kyiv and elsewhere in Ukraine overnight, authorities said. Zelenskyy was in New York for the annual U.N. gathering as part of his diplomatic effort to shore up and recruit further international support for his country’s grueling 4½-year fight against Russia’s invasion. He addressed the General Assembly, met with European leaders and was also due to hold talks with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte. In his address to the Assembly, Zelenskyy urged the international community to keep limiting Russian oil revenues to prevent Russia’s ability to keep financing its war in Ukraine. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy speaks during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at United Nations headquarters, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. (AP Photo/Heather Khalifa) “When someone gives Russia more money through trade, they give this war more time. And that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia’s revenues ourselves,” he said. Zelenskyy met on Tuesday with U.S. President Donald Trump, who has shown impatience with the lack of progress in talks aimed at ending the war and the escalating aerial attacks by both sides this year. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Wednesday that there are “no concrete plans” for a high-level meeting between U.S. and Russian officials that might help break the deadlock in negotiations. He insisted that Moscow is “open to peace talks.” Russian President Vladimir Putin, who has been accused by NATO officials and European governments of sabotage, espionage and other threats, is not scheduled to attend the U.N. gathering this year. ADVERTISEMENT The Polish military said a Russian military helicopter briefly violated Poland’s airspace Wednesday on the country’s border with Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave. It said that “the nature of the incident suggests that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense.” Ukraine has hit back at Russia by damaging oil refineries that are a vital pillar of the country’s economy. Speaking in New York, Zelenskyy said Russia’s oil, gasoline, diesel and ports were not Ukraine’s objective. “Our target is Russia’s ability to finance this war, to drag it out, to make it more brutal and more destructive. Russia’s finances and Russia’s production are what must be stopped,” he said. ADVERTISEMENT Zelenskyy said at the start of his U.S. visit that he had proposals for a possible de-escalation in the war. Urgent issues for Kyiv are halting devastating Russian strikes on Ukraine’s power grid and ensuring Ukrainian grain can be shipped to world markets through the Black Sea despite the war. Ukraine also needs more U.S.-made Patriot air defense systems as a shield against Russian ballistic missiles, but Patriots are in short supply after the war in Iran began. In Zaporizhzhia, in southeastern Ukraine, two men aged 37 and 39 were wounded by a strike that started a large fire at a shopping mall. Emergency services said the fire spread across about 6,000 square meters (1.5 acres) before coming under control. The Russian Defense Ministry said that its forces struck Ukraine’s military-industrial and energy sector facilities, logistics centers and sea vessels in overnight attacks. The ministry said its air defenses intercepted more than 500 Ukrainian drones over multiple Russian regions, as well as illegally annexed Crimea and waters of the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. Manage Preferences The division in Latvian society along ethnic lines is greater in our perceptions than in reality, according to the association "Russian Voice for Latvia", after surveying almost 600 Latvian residents on the streets and online this year. Their aim was to determine the attitudes of both Latvian and Russian speakers towards various issues polarizing society, as well as the attitudes of members of these groups towards each other. Martins Levuškāns, chairman of the board of the association "Russian Voice for Latvia", says that the idea for the study was borrowed from the United States, where a similar study was conducted comparing Democratic and Republican supporters. That survey also revealed that the differences were not as great as is commonly thought. Part of such perceptions are shaped by what is read and seen on social media, where the most vocal tend to be the most radical. Since the study participants were asked not only their opinion, but also what they thought the representatives of the other group thought about the issue in question, this is a 'metapolarization study' conducted for the first time in Latvia. "The main thing we find is that the difference in perceptions is much greater than the difference in reality. News, politicians' statements, and much more influence not only what people think, but how they think other people think. The difference in opinions is much smaller than people think," says Levuškāns. For example, on a scale of 1 to 10, where the higher the score, the more positive the attitude, regarding Latvia's membership in the European Union (EU), Latvians' attitude was rated at 8.4 points, while the Russian-speaking opinion is 7. The position on Latvia's membership in NATO is more diverse: Latvians gave 8.7 points, while Russian-speakers gave it three points less. Attitudes towards support for Ukraine also differ. Latvians believe that Ukraine should receive even more help, while Russian-speakers mostly think that the help is too much. The researchers themselves also admit that it could be that at least some of the respondents gave what they thought was a socially acceptable answer, rather than revealing their true thoughts. "I mentioned social norms when specifically talking about the issue of refugees from Ukraine. It's uncomfortable to talk about, and it's known that some Russian speakers would rather not talk about this topic at all, but in principle, I think we were lucky that people were open," says Ramona Safkulieva, one of the study's authors. Despite differences in opinion, the attitudes of both groups towards each other are mostly positive. The average score for Latvians' attitude towards Russian speakers was 7.3, while Russian speakers' assessment of Latvians reached 8.5 points. It is true that both Latvians and Russian-speakers think that the other group's attitude towards them is not so positive. According to Russian-speakers, Latvians' perception of them is only at the level of 5.1 points, while Russians give them 6.6 points in Latvian perceptions. The study participants were also asked to what extent they were willing to socialize with members of the other group. It turned out that both groups were favourable in this regard. Latvian speakers rated their child's friendship with a child from a Russian-speaking family with 7.9 points, while Russian speakers were even more positive about their child's friendship with a Latvian, scoring an average of 8.8 points. The study also concluded that Russian-speaking people have a more tolerant attitude towards immigrants from India than those whose native language is Latvian. Russian Voice for Latvia describes itself as "a democratic organization whose aim is to build a strong and united Latvian political nation, promote social cohesion, support the social inclusion of minorities, and strengthen democracy and the fundamental values of the European Union."
